title: Introduce graft-and-relocate stitching layer to adapt CUTLASS/Triton symbol mismatches
creator: Alyssa Chen
description: Problem: Upgrading to CUDA 13.x and Triton 3.x has exposed a class of subtle ABI and symbol-level mismatches with CUTLASS-based kernels. These mismatches cause rare cold-start failures and non-deterministic fallback paths on heterogeneous fleets. Existing approaches (static shims or full kernel re-linking) are heavy-weight, brittle, and slow to iterate. Goal: Implement a lightweight runtime 'graft-and-relocate' stitching layer that can: 1) detect missing or incompatible exported symbols at process start or module load, 2) dynamically emit small thunk/adapter symbols that translate caller expectations to available kernel APIs (callsite granularity), and 3) record deterministic relocation patches that can be cached and replayed across restarts and deployments. This feature should reduce cold-start error rate, avoid full binary re-bundling for most model revisions, and enable faster Canary rollouts when CUTLASS/Triton patches are deployed.
updates: 2025-10-22 - AC: Scoped spike completed. Prototype successfully intercepts missing symbol 'cutlass::gemm::schedule' and provides a callsite adapter that forwards to 'cutlass::gemm::dispatch_v2' with lightweight argument marshaling. Measured probe overhead ~120us per process startup in debug build.

2025-11-05 - DM: Design doc posted in Confluence: /redwood/runtime/graft-relocate-stitcher. Key design decisions: (a) prefer callsite thunks vs full ABI shims to minimize surface area, (b) maintain immutable relocation-log artifact per node image for reproducibility, (c) integrate with existing kernel-probe cache for fast warm starts.

2025-11-18 - PR #12283 opened: initial implementation of runtime graft table and relocation-log writer. Unit tests for symbol discovery and deterministic serialization added. CI failing on macOS cross-build (expected).

2025-12-02 - DM: Microbench harness created: gpu-compat-harness repo/folders/graft. End-to-end test shows 98.7% reduction in symbol-mismatch fallbacks in our Triton 3.0 -> 3.1 canary fleet (canary: 40 nodes). Throughput regression measured <0.6% for steady-state inference after grafting is applied.

2026-01-14 - LK (SRE): Deployment experiment on dedicated-dev cluster succeeded. Recorded relocation-log artifacts in artifact-store (s3://redwood-artifacts/graft/2026-01-14). Observability hooks added to Console: per-node graft applied flag and relocation-log size metric.

2026-02-03 - DM: Added safety mode 'validate-only' used by CI to verify graft tables without applying them. This helped catch an edge-case where template-param mismatches required small type conversion at callsite.
2026-02-20 - AC: Performance note: JIT thunk emission moved to a background worker to avoid extending critical process startup path. Cold-start probe now completes within SLAs on 98% of test images.
2026-03-04 - PR #13011 merged: deterministic relocation replay, cache eviction policy, and integration with the kernel-probe-cache. Rolling canary to staging fleet next week.

2026-03-10 - DM: Blocker identified: one legacy on-prem image uses a custom CUTLASS build with renamed namespaces; graft layer can adapt but requires a per-tenant mapping table. Tracking as follow-up sub-issue ENG-762002.
